ai.definition: Industrial robots are programmable, automated machines designed to perform various manufacturing tasks with high precision and repeatability.
ai.howItWorks: Industrial robots use servo motors to control their movements and can integrate with machine vision systems for enhanced accuracy. They follow predefined paths or adapt based on programmed instructions to complete tasks such as welding, painting, assembly, and material handling.
ai.problemSolved: They address the need for increased efficiency, precision, and consistency in manufacturing processes, reducing human error and improving productivity.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves assembling components from various materials like metals, plastics, and electronics. The process includes programming the robot's movements, calibrating sensors, and integrating with other machinery on the production line.
ai.buildProcess: The build process starts with designing the robot according to specific requirements, followed by assembly using precision tools and equipment. Testing is conducted to ensure all functions operate correctly before deployment in a manufacturing environment.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include initial investment for purchasing robots, ongoing maintenance costs, energy consumption, and programming complexity. Training operators also contributes significantly to overall expenses.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as industrial robotics continue to gain traction in various industries due to increasing demand for automation solutions.
ai.regulation: Regulations vary by region but generally focus on safety standards, environmental impact assessments, and worker training requirements. Compliance with international standards like ISO 10218-1 helps ensure safe operation of robots.
ai.risks: Risks include equipment failure leading to production downtime, data security concerns related to robotic systems, and potential job displacement for human workers in certain industries.
ai.profitability: Profitability can be high for companies that successfully implement industrial robotics, as they often lead to significant cost savings through increased efficiency and reduced labor costs. However, initial setup costs may deter some smaller businesses from adopting this technology.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development trends include advancements in artificial intelligence (AI) integration, collaborative robots (cobots), and enhanced sensor technologies for improved precision and adaptability in dynamic manufacturing environments.

glossary.def: Electromechanical devices that convert electrical signals into precise mechanical movements, used to control the motion of industrial robots.
A technology that uses cameras and software to interpret visual information from the environment, enabling robots to perform tasks requiring high accuracy and precision.
Robotic systems designed to work alongside humans in shared spaces, enhancing productivity while ensuring safety through advanced sensor technologies and programming capabilities.

subsystems.name: Manipulator structure
subsystems.role: the arm itself: rigid links connected by joints that position the tool in space.

subsystems.name: Joint drives
subsystems.role: convert electrical power into precise rotary motion at each joint.

subsystems.name: Controller and motion software
subsystems.role: computes the joint angles needed to reach a commanded position and time.

subsystems.name: End effector
subsystems.role: the tool that actually does the work.

subsystems.name: Sensing
subsystems.role: lets the robot know where it is and what it is touching.

subsystems.name: Safety system
subsystems.role: keeps people safe when the arm moves fast and carries momentum.

buildSteps.title: Fix the kinematics and duty
buildSteps.detail: Choose the number of axes, reach in metres, payload in kilograms, and repeatability as a fraction of a millimetre, based on the task.

buildSteps.title: Make the links
buildSteps.detail: Cast or machine aluminium or steel into arm sections, then bore and finish the bearing seats so joints align precisely.

buildSteps.title: Build joint modules
buildSteps.detail: Assemble motor, reducer, brake and encoder into a sealed unit; the reducer removes backlash so the arm repeats its position.

buildSteps.title: Stack the arm
buildSteps.detail: Bolt joint modules and links together, route cables internally, and add counterbalancing so the motors are not overloaded.

buildSteps.title: Wire and integrate the controller
buildSteps.detail: Connect drives to the controller, tune current, velocity and position loops, and load the kinematic model of the arm.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Zero each joint, measure actual link lengths, set the tool centre point, and test repeatability with a dial gauge or laser tracker.

buildSteps.title: Validate safety
buildSteps.detail: Carry out a risk assessment, install fencing or scanners, and verify emergency stop, speed limits and safe stopping distances.

buildSteps.title: Program and hand over
buildSteps.detail: Teach paths or load CAM-generated programs, integrate the gripper and vision, and run production trials before signing off.

prerequisites.why: accurate positioning depends on motors that continuously correct against encoder feedback.
harmonic and cycloidal gears give high torque with very low backlash, which is what makes repeatability possible.
trajectories must be recalculated thousands of times per second to move smoothly.
letting a robot find and handle parts that are not in exactly the same place remains harder than blind repetition.
power-and-force limiting and safety-rated monitoring allow robots to work beside people without full cages.

pathway.milestone: high-speed, caged arms welding, painting, picking and assembling in factories
pathway.unlocks: consistent mass production at low unit cost.

pathway.milestone: collaborative arms with force sensing and easier programming
pathway.unlocks: automation for small and medium workshops.

pathway.milestone: mobile manipulators — an arm on an autonomous mobile base
pathway.unlocks: machine tending, warehouse picking and logistics tasks.

pathway.milestone: learning-based task planning from demonstration or language
pathway.unlocks: robots that can be retasked quickly for new products rather than reprogrammed by specialists.
